data.text: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it, together with all its furnishings, the altar, and all its utensils. He anointed them and consecrated them.
data.titulo: Gifts for the Service of the Tabernacle

data.text: The leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral households, presented offerings. They were the leaders of the tribes, the men who oversaw those registered.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen, a cart for every two leaders and an ox for each one. They presented them before the tabernacle.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
“Receive these from them for performing the service of the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, each according to his service.”
Moses received the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the descendants of Gershon, according to their service.
He gave four carts and eight oxen to the descendants of Merari, according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave none to the descendants of Kohath, because the service of the holy things was their charge; they were to carry them on their shoulders.
The leaders presented the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders presented their offering before the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, “They shall present their offering for the dedication of the altar, one leader each day, one leader each day.”
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.
data.subtitulo: The Offerings of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun

data.text: His offering was one silver dish weighing about three and a quarter pounds and one silver bowl weighing about one and three-quarter pounds, according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold ladle weighing about four ounces, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, presented his offering.

He presented as his offering one silver dish weighing about three and a quarter pounds and one silver bowl weighing about one and three-quarter pounds, according to the sanctuary weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold ladle weighing about four ounces, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the descendants of Zebulun, presented his offering.

On the fourth day Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the descendants of Reuben, presented his offering.

This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel on the day it was anointed: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold ladles.

Each silver dish weighed about three and a quarter pounds, and each bowl about one and three-quarter pounds. All the silver of the vessels weighed about sixty pounds, according to the sanctuary weight.
The twelve gold ladles were filled with incense, each weighing about four ounces according to the sanctuary weight. All the gold of the ladles weighed about three pounds.
All the cattle for the burnt offering were twelve bulls; the rams were twelve, and the year-old male lambs twelve, with their grain offering. There were twelve male goats for a sin offering.

All the cattle for the sacrifice of peace offerings were twenty-four bulls, with sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty year-old male lambs. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.
When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony, from between the two cherubim. And he spoke to him.
data.titulo: The LORD Speaks from the Tent of Meeting
